Bill.BriefDescription: Making possession of motorcycle theft tools a crime.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to possession of motorcycle theft tools; adding anew section to chapter 9A.56 RCW; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.56 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Every person who possesses, gives, or lends any device designedto bypass the factory installed ignition of a motorcycle in order tostart the engine of a motorcycle without a manufacturer's key, with theintent to unlawfully take or drive, or to facilitate the unlawfultaking or driving of, a motorcycle without the consent of the owner isguilty of a gross misdemeanor. (2) Every person who possesses, gives, or lends any item ofhardware including, but not limited to, bolt cutters, electrical tape,wire cutters, wire strippers, or allen wrenches, with the intent tounlawfully take or drive, or to facilitate the unlawful taking ordriving of, a motorcycle without the consent of the owner is guilty ofa gross misdemeanor. (3) For purposes of this section, "device" includes any motorcycle p. 1 SHB 1542ignition, or any part thereof, an altered motorcycle ignition known asa pigtail, and a secondary ignition.
